  "title": "Delete tickets via admin interface as job",
  "body": "Please make it possible to delete tickets and not just close them. :smile_cat: \n",

      "id": 254849584,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-254849584",
      "created_at": "2016-10-19T15:32:12Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "Hi @MDXDave - since Zammad is revision-proof this is not an option.\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 254850325,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-254850325",
      "created_at": "2016-10-19T15:34:28Z",
      "updated_at": "2016-10-19T15:35:47Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "I understand your objection, but at least admins should have the possibility to delete tickets.\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 254851061,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-254851061",
      "created_at": "2016-10-19T15:36:57Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "As an admin you can use the `rails c` command on the command line. From there on you can go and do whatever possibilities rails is giving you. Tickets can get deleted via `Ticket.find(*id*).destroy`. Hope that helps? We do not recommend that.\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 254851964,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-254851964",
      "created_at": "2016-10-19T15:39:40Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "I know that this is possible with rails, but it would be easier to delete tickets within Zammad. :+1: \n"
    },
    {
      "id": 254976420,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-254976420",
      "created_at": "2016-10-20T00:14:37Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "At least scheduler should be able to do it.\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 255031098,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-255031098",
      "created_at": "2016-10-20T07:35:03Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "I think @thorsteneckel decision is right. You should be able to audit old tickets after years so deletion shouldn't be an option at least in the UI. For testing zammad (even a production setup) you should be fine using the rails console which is not hard as well!\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 255075721,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-255075721",
      "created_at": "2016-10-20T11:03:14Z",
      "updated_at": "2016-10-20T11:03:28Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "I use this function in OTRS to delete spam tickets after 30 days in our spam queue. Sure, one could do this from the command line but its not so comfortable like to do it from the scheduler.\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 256579029,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-256579029",
      "created_at": "2016-10-27T08:25:46Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "I see your point! We will implement it in the near future. Maybe something like https://github.com/rubysherpas/paranoia is useful in this context.\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 258707242,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-258707242",
      "created_at": "2016-11-06T20:15:11Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "It's not only about hiding the tickets,it's also about removing the unnecessary stuff from the DB. Currently our spam to ham mail ratio is pretty high, but we detect most of the messages with spamassassin. Nevertheless, email filtering happens after downloading the mails from the POP3, so the tickets have already been created the database and the disk space allocated (speaking of OTRS)\nOne solution could be to store a reference to the ticket, and replace the content by the information that the ticket has been deleted. So in case of an audit you can prove that the ticket was created, but no longer exists ?\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 259426969,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-259426969",
      "created_at": "2016-11-09T14:28:37Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 11",
      "body": "Is there any documentation of how to get in and use the rails console?\n\nI'm currently testing a lot around, and I'd like to get rid of all the tickets \"Test1\", \"Test2\", \"Test3\" etc ;-)\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 259445976,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-259445976",
      "created_at": "2016-11-09T15:45:03Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 12",
      "body": "> Is there any documentation of how to get in and use the rails console?\n\nshell> rails c\nrails> Ticket.destroy_all\n\nIf you use the Zammad RPM, you need to do:\nshell> zammad run rails c\nrails> Ticket.destroy_all\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 259457967,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-259457967",
      "created_at": "2016-11-09T16:29:47Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 11",
      "body": "Thanks, works like a charm!\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 280607764,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-280607764",
      "created_at": "2017-02-17T10:00:12Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 13",
      "body": "in case you're looking for a way to delete all tickets but some you can use this method:\r\n\r\n```ruby\r\ntickets_to_keep = [1, 2, 3] # enter the ids of all tickets you want to keep\r\n(Ticket.all.pluck(:id) - tickets_to_keep).each { |id| Ticket.find(id).destroy }\r\n```\r\n\r\nthis will delete all tickets **except** Ticket with id `1`, `2` and `3`"
    },
    {
      "id": 286311495,

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "Still no news about it? 😐"

      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "Hello @passboltUser ,\r\ni think you just missclicked.\r\n\r\n* Click on the menu **Scheduler**\r\n* Then on the top right on **New scheduler**\r\n* Below you choose the time where the tickets should get deleted.\r\n* Below you choose the conditions for the deletion of the tickets\r\n* Below you see some example tickets which will get deleted\r\n* Below you see the action you can do on the tickets. Here you can choose **Action -> Delete**\r\n\r\n![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5445062/33309519-a3b48816-d41e-11e7-8c12-e0980f91d4ea.png)\r\n\r\nBest regards,\r\n\r\n-------------------------------------------\r\n\r\nHallo @passboltUser ,\r\nich glaube du hast dich nur verklickt.\r\n\r\n* Klick mal auf **Automatisierungen**\r\n* Dann rechts oben auf **Neue zeitgesteuerte Aktion**\r\n* Dann wählst du als erstes den Zeitpunkt aus wann die Tickets immer gelöscht werden\r\n* Darunter die Bedingungen die ein Ticket erhalten muss damit es gelöscht wird\r\n* Darunter sieht man einen Ausschnitt der Liste der Tickets die dann gelöscht wird.\r\n* Und darunter sieht man die Aktion, welche bei den Tickets ausgeführt werden soll. Hier wählst du dann \r\n**Aktion -> Löschen** aus.\r\n\r\n![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5445062/33308701-c56cd1dc-d41b-11e7-8157-8770e0dc85b7.png)\r\n\r\nGruß\r\n\r\n"

      "id": 368075607,
      "url": "https://github.com/zammad/zammad/issues/214#issuecomment-368075607",
      "created_at": "2018-02-23T17:16:25Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 8",
      "body": "First, i am happy to be able to delete tickets that creates loops - like tickets out techs sent to wrong email address of the client and the NDR keeps returning as we try to close the ticket since there is a close notification...\r\n\r\nThe problem we face is having a batch of 30 different numbered tickets that has loops or other issues that we want to delete and the schedule way is a way to learn what is patience... one manually entered ticket number for every 5 minutes...\r\n\r\nMy 2c is that there should be an admin-only, password protected form to delete tickets directly at the web interface."
    },
